title: Metadata tied to particular timestamps
statement: As a bioimage analyst,\nI want to save metadata tied to particular timestamps,\nso we can correctly process data acquired in non-uniform sampling protocols, used in e.g. long time lapses and smart microscopy setups.
workaround: RFC-5 coordinate transform mapping frames to acquisition time
notes: 0.5: No coordinates transform in 0.5; frame times and events need custom attributes.\n0.6: Awkward: Frame-to-time mapping fits a `coordinates` transformation, but its array must be a valid multiscale image with 2 or 3 space axes, so a plain 1D time lookup is not allowed; it needs dummy spatial axes. Arbitrary metadata tied to timepoints (events) has no place in the spec.\n0.9dev: Suggestion: timestamps work as in STORY-002 (Possible), but event metadata still has no place.

title: Timestamps for non-uniform temporal sampling
statement:
As a bioimage analyst working with live-imaging data,
I want to store a timestamp for each frame,
so that non-uniformly sampled time lapses are visualized and processed (e.g. velocity estimation) correctly.

Original: As an image analyst working with live-imaging data I encounter data that is non-uniformly sampled in time. This could be due to interruptions in long-term acquisitions or experimentally preferred variable sampling rates (e.g., lower sampling rate early on when a sample is more susceptible to photo-toxicity, event based changes to sampling rate in a smart microscopy setting). I want to store per-frame timestamps that allow correct visualization and processing (e.g., velocity estimation) of the data. The example stores POSIX timestamps as a parquet table, or as an array in the DCA metadata. In OME-Zarr v0.6 an alternative would be to use a RFC-5 coordinates transform.
workaround: RFC-5 coordinates (time array); else parquet table or custom attributes
notes:
0.5: Time can only be scaled uniformly (scale/translation); per-frame timestamps need custom attributes.
0.6: Awkward: Same as STORY-001: per-frame timestamps can be a `coordinates` transformation on the time axis, padded with spatial axes to satisfy the multiscale constraints. Workable, but nothing is dedicated to it.
0.9dev: Suggestion: RFC-3 lifts the 2–3 space axes rule, so a 1D `coordinates` lookup on t works without dummy axes; looks Possible rather than Unsure.
Forum (60885): 2022 call: unequally spaced time and unitless 'cycle' dimensions for multi-cycle imaging.
Zulip (potential RFC: coordinate arrays): irregular timepoints as a 1D coordinate array next to the data; RFC-5 `coordinates` transforms cover part of it.
Zulip (potential RFC: coordinate arrays): in slow scans the acquisition time also varies within a frame (per plane or per sample).

title: Some channels only imaged at certain time points
statement:
As a bioimage analyst in a core facility,
I want to store time lapses where some channels are acquired only at some timepoints,
so that sparse channels are kept without padding them with zeros.

Original: As a bioimage analyst in a microscopy core facility, I came across the following problem: I want to convert time lapse data generated by a high-content screening microscope to ome-zarr. The problem is that some channels are acquired at all time points, while other channels are only acquired at some time points. This is to reduce the amount of acquired data, as not all channels are needed for time-dependent analysis. The question is now how best to save this into ome-zarr. Should all channels be saved into one zarr-array with the missing time-points / channels as zeros? Or should the channels be saved in separate arrays and connected with appropriate transforms?
notes: 0.5: No scene: channel groups can be separate entries in the `multiscales` list (or bioformats2raw series), each with its own axes, but nothing relates them.\n0.6: Store the channel groups as separate images, each with its own time axis and scale, related in a `scene`. One image with sparse channels is not possible: every channel shares the same time axis.\n0.9dev: As 0.6: separate images in a `scene`, each with its own time axis.

title: Some channels as z-stacks, others as single planes
statement:
As a bioimage analyst in a core facility,
I want to store images where some channels are z-stacks and others single planes or projections,
so that 2D channels are kept without padding and shared metadata is written once.

Original: As a bioimage analyst in a microscopy core facility, I came across the following problem: I want to convert data generated by a high-content screening microscope to ome-zarr. The problem is that for some channels the entire z-stack is saved, while for other channels only a single 2D image is saved. They can either be a single z-slice, or a projected image. This is to reduce the amount of acquired data, as not all channels are needed for 3D analysis. The question is now how best to save this into ome-zarr. Should all channels be saved into one zarr-array with the missing z-slices / channels as zeros? Or should the channels be saved in separate arrays and connected with appropriate transforms? Usually the same metadata will apply to the 2D image as the z-stack. Is there a place to write this once and reference across the two zarr files? Is this solved by collections/RFC-8?
notes: 0.5: No scene or projectAxis: the 2D channels can be stored as a separate 3D image with one z plane, but linking it to the 3D image is implicit.\n0.6: Store the 3D and 2D channels as separate images in a `scene`; `projectAxis` (createdOutputs) places the 2D image in the 3D space. Metadata shared by both images cannot be written once: there is no shared or collection-level metadata.\n0.9dev: As 0.6: separate images in a `scene`, `projectAxis` places the 2D image.

title: Per-timepoint normalization statistics and annotations
statement:
As a data scientist,
I want to store summary statistics and annotations (e.g. an intervention time) per dataset and per timepoint,
so that I and downstream users can normalize data without reading the full images.

Original: As a data scientist, I may want to pre-compute and store summary statistics at the dataset level or per timepoint when processing images. This is helpful so that I (or other downstream users) can later apply different types of data normalization approaches efficiently without reading full images. It’s also possible there might be other timepoint annotations, such as timestamps or the timepoint of an ablation or intervention, that I want to save. There isn’t a convention for how to store these timepoint annotations or statistics in ome-zarr or other metadata that are indexed by timepoint. Where should these data be stored? If you have a lot of timepoints, this can make the zarr.json really large and overcrowd other metadata stored there. It could be saved in a tabular format as well or as an array. Also, how do we want to index time? Should we use frames or the origin timestamp + gap from the previous frame (relevant to the non-uniform temporal sampling story as well)? How does this impact downsampled arrays?
notes:
0.5: No tables or per-timepoint annotations.
0.6: No tables and no per-timepoint annotations in 0.6; only custom attributes or side files.
0.9dev: No tables or per-timepoint annotations.
Forum (33410): computing a histogram of a 300 GB volume is hard; precomputed statistics would help.
Zulip (per array contrast limits): per-timestep contrast limits for a multichannel 3D+t array are too costly to compute on the fly; there is no place for metadata that grows with an axis.

title: Biological annotations for channels
statement:
As a data scientist working across a large repository,
I want to record what each channel shows (type, target, marker, or a free-text description),
so that pipelines can find channels by meaning instead of by position.

Original: As a data scientist, I would like to index and record the type of channel and relevant biology in a dataset. While most processing pipelines assume a fixed, ordered set of channels, this breaks down across a large repository of data. For some channel types (i.e. fluorescence), it’s helpful to include target, marker, labeled structures, labeled molecules, or marker type. For other channel types (i.e. label-free), simple free-text descriptions could work. How does the community want to reference and look up biological relevant annotations (i.e. by name or index)? What is the core model that’s relevant for all channels? In an HCS plate, this information may be duplicated many times within a zarr. Where is this information stored? Is there a way to only reference it once?
workaround: DCA channel-metadata spec
notes:
0.5: Only `omero` channel `label`; the rest is custom.
0.6: Only the transitional `omero` channel `label` exists; target, marker and structure need custom attributes. No way to declare it once per plate.
0.9dev: Only `omero` channel `label`.
Zulip (per-channel metadata after `omero` key is phased out): after `omero` is phased out, users want per-channel ontology terms (e.g. UniProt IDs for antibody targets, UBERON terms for label channels).

title: Linear intensity calibration
statement:
As a bioimage analyst in a core facility,
I want to describe intensity corrections such as background subtraction and linear scaling,
so that images are calibrated without altering or duplicating the data.

Original: As a bioimage analyst in a microscopy core facility,
I want to have calibrated intensity values of my images. I would like to apply different corrections, like subtraction of a constant background value, and linear scaling of intensities. One example would be, that we want to compensate for varying instrument sensitivity over long periods of time. We can track the instrument performance with reference measurements and then correct the images accordingly. Burning these corrections into the data has several downsides, like duplication / alteration of data, or reduction in intensity resolution (when rounding floats to integers). Therefore, it would be great, if these intensity calibrations could be described in the spec somewhere.
notes: 0.5: No intensity transformations.\n0.6: No intensity transformations in the spec. `omero` `coefficient`/`family` are display settings only.\n0.9dev: No intensity transformations.

title: Nonlinear intensity calibration
statement:
As a bioimage analyst in a core facility,
I want to describe a detector's non-linear response curve,
so that intensities are calibrated without altering or duplicating the data.

Original: As a bioimage analyst in a microscopy core facility,
I want to have calibrated intensity values of my images. For example, a detector can have a non-linear response to the incoming light intensity, i.e. it is less efficient at high photon count rates. If I have a calibration curve of the detector, I can account for this. Burning these corrections into the data has several downsides, like duplication / alteration of data, or reduction in intensity resolution (when rounding floats to integers). Therefore, it would be great, if these intensity calibrations could be described in the spec somewhere.
notes: 0.5: No intensity transformations.\n0.6: No intensity transformations in the spec; a calibration curve needs custom attributes or an extra array.\n0.9dev: No intensity transformations.

title: Spatially varying intensity correction
statement:
As a bioimage analyst in a core facility,
I want to describe a flatfield correction for uneven illumination,
so that it is applied without altering or duplicating the data.

Original: As a bioimage analyst in a microscopy core facility,
I want to be able to account for inhomogeneous illumination. Microscopes often have inhomogeneous illumination across the field of view. One can account for this by dividing the image by a reference “flatfield” image. Burning these corrections into the data leads to duplication / alteration of the original data. Therefore, it would be great, if these corrections could be described in the spec somewhere.
notes: 0.5: No intensity correction.\n0.6: No intensity correction in the spec. The flatfield can be stored as another image, but linking it as a correction is custom.\n0.9dev: No intensity correction.

title: Metadata at different collection levels
statement:
As a data producer,
I want to attach metadata to a whole set of images (e.g. one specimen) and other metadata to only a subset (e.g. one perturbation condition),
so that each piece of metadata is recorded once, at the level where it applies.

Original: Related to biological DCA metadata, I might want to write some components associated with a set of movies (e.g., generated in one acquisition all containing the same biological specimen) and others with only a subset of them (e.g., perturbation conditions within an experiment).
notes: 0.5: Only plate, well and the transitional bioformats2raw layout; other collections are custom.\n0.6: 0.6 has no metadata for arbitrary collections (only plate, well, scene and the transitional bioformats2raw layout); anything else is custom attributes on a group.\n0.9dev: Only plate, well, scene and bioformats2raw; RFC-8 collections not in this draft.

title: Per-coordinate transforms along c and t
statement:
As an image analyst and pipeline developer,
I want to apply a different transform per timepoint or per channel,
so that drift correction and channel alignment are stored without resampling.

Original: As an image analyst and microscopy pipeline developer,
I want to be able to apply different transforms to different coordinates along a non-spatial image dimension of an existing image,
so that I can save the transformations resulting from processing steps such as the following in OME-Zarr transformation metadata, avoiding the need for resampling of the image data: drift correction (one transformation per coordinate along dim t); channel alignment (one transformation per coordinate along dim c).

Note: RFC5 mentions the by-coordinate transformation in "future possibilities".
workaround: Resample data; RFC-5 lists by-coordinate transforms as future possibility
notes:
0.5: 0.5 has only scale and translation transforms, applied to the whole array; no per-channel or per-timepoint transforms.
0.6: Awkward: Along t: a `displacements` field indexed by time (with coarse spatial sampling) can hold one shift per timepoint, without resampling. Along c: not inside one image, since a transformation applies to the whole array; channels must be split into separate images in a `scene`, each with its own transform.
0.9dev: As 0.6; RFC-3 removes the dummy-axis problem for fields, but per-channel transforms still need channels split into separate images.
Zulip (per-channel metadata after `omero` key is phased out): feedback-microscopy users try to fit per-timepoint transforms into the format.

title: Large-scale tile stitching
statement:
As a developer of tile stitching methods,
I want to add new transformation types and keep alignments separate from the image data,
so that new registration methods can be stored without a spec revision and several alignment solutions can be compared.

Original: As a method developer for stitching large scale tiles, I would want the following:
1. extend the spec with additional transformation types, so that new registration methods (e.g. non-rigid or other models) can be represented without waiting for a core spec revision.
2. alignment information to live separately from the image data, so that I can compare multiple alignment solutions and compare them.
notes:
0.5: 0.5 has only scale and translation transforms; alignments cannot be stored apart from the images.
0.6: A `scene` can hold several alignments as transforms and coordinate systems, but it must live in the same Zarr hierarchy as the tiles; truly separate alignments come with RFC-8 collections. New transformation types are not supported: only the listed types are valid, so a non-rigid model outside them is custom (or approximated by a displacement field).
0.9dev: Only the listed transformation types are valid. RFC-8 would add prefixed extension types (e.g. myorg:nonlinear) and collections that reference tiles by path.
Zulip (OME-ZARR and overlapping tiles): thousands to millions of overlapping tiles; one JSON document gets too large, so a collection could be a data model with other serialisations.

title: Images with different Z-ranges in one dataset
statement:
As a bioimaging data repository developer,
I want to store channels acquired over different z-ranges in one dataset, spatially aligned,
so that users view and analyse them together.

Original: As a bioimaging data repository developer,
I want to represent fluorescence and bright-field images acquired over different Z-ranges within a single OME-Zarr dataset while preserving their spatial alignment,
so that users can visualize and analyze both images together without treating them as separate datasets.

Background and current limitations: in the dataset, fluorescence images were acquired across Z-planes 0-50, while bright-field images were acquired only at Z-planes 22-30. OME-Zarr 0.5 does not provide a standardized way to represent these images with different Z-ranges as a single spatially aligned dataset.

Possible solutions: this use case can be addressed using Scenes in OME-Zarr 0.6, which allow images with different dimensions to be grouped while preserving their spatial relationships.
workaround: Scenes (RFC-5)
notes: 0.5: No scene, but separate images (e.g. bioformats2raw series) with their own scale and translation share an implicit physical space.\n0.6: `scene` groups images of different shapes and keeps them aligned.

title: Link segmentations to their source channels
statement:
As a bioimage or medical image analyst,
I want to store several, possibly overlapping or channel-specific, segmentations with an image and say what each one is,
so that none are lost and tools know which belongs to which channel.

Original: As a bioimage or medical image analyst,
I want to store several segmentations of the same image (including overlapping ones and ones tied to specific image channels) together with my OME-Zarr image, and record what each one is and which channel it comes from,
so that overlapping structures (e.g. nucleus and cell, organ and tumor) and channel-specific segmentations are kept without loss, and other people and tools can tell which segmentation belongs to which channel without guessing from names.
notes: 0.5: `image-label` `source` points to an image, not a channel.\n0.6: Several, overlapping label images are Core (`labels` group). `image-label` `source` points to an image but not to a channel, so which channel a label comes from needs a custom key.\n0.9dev: `image-label` `source` points to an image, not a channel.

title: Multiscale levels in different storages
statement:
As a data provider hosting large images,
I want resolution levels to live in different filesets or locations,
so that previews load fast and levels can be added or moved without rewriting the image.

Original: As a data provider hosting large images,
I want the resolution levels of an image to be able to sit in different filesets or locations (e.g. full resolution in archive storage, smaller levels on a fast server),
so that viewers can load previews quickly, and I can add or move resolution levels without copying or rewriting the whole image.
notes:
0.5: `datasets` paths are relative to the multiscales group.
0.6: `datasets` paths are relative to the multiscales group, so all levels live in the same hierarchy; levels elsewhere would break the multiscales definition.
0.9dev: `datasets` paths are relative to the multiscales group.
Zurich 2026 links discussion: lossily-compressed downscales hosted separately should point to the original as base level.

title: Segmentations stored separately from the image
statement:
As a bioimage analyst working with public images,
I want to save my segmentations in my own fileset and link them to the original image,
so that I can create and share labels without write access to the original data or copying large images, and viewers can show image and labels together.

Also included: the need for "viewers to overlay a source OME-Zarr and a separate annotation/labels OME-Zarr at display time" (Mandloi2309, ngff#78) and ngff#42.
notes:
0.5: Labels must sit in the image `labels` group; external links are custom.
0.6: Label images must sit in the image's own `labels` group. A separate fileset can hold a valid OME-Zarr image, but linking it to the original is custom.
0.9dev: Labels must sit in the image `labels` group.
Zurich 2026 links discussion: publish labels for raw data on someone else's S3 without re-hosting it.

title: Default color and contrast per channel
statement:
As a bioimage data producer sharing multi-channel images,
I want to save a display color and contrast limits (display range) for each channel with my data,
so that any viewer opens the image looking the way I intended, and users don’t have to adjust every channel by hand.

Note: covered by the omero transitional metadata in OME-Zarr 0.6.
workaround: omero transitional metadata
notes: 0.5: Core extension (transitional omero metadata): `color` and `window` start/end.\n0.6: Core extension (transitional omero metadata): `omero` channels `color` and `window` start/end.\n0.9dev: Core extension (was marked Transitional before the scale changed).

title: Channels shown by default
statement: As a user opening images with many channels (e.g. 50+ in multiplexed imaging), I want the data to say which channels are switched on when the image first opens, so that I start from a readable view instead of an overlay of every channel, and the same channels show up in every viewer.\n\nNote: covered by the omero transitional metadata in OME-Zarr 0.6.
workaround: omero transitional metadata
notes: 0.5: Core extension (transitional omero metadata): `active`.\n0.6: Core extension (transitional omero metadata): `omero` channels `active`.\n0.9dev: Core extension (was marked Transitional before the scale changed).

title: Intensity range for display controls
statement:
As a viewer developer,
I want to know the meaningful intensity range of each channel (e.g. the actual minimum and maximum pixel values), separate from the default contrast,
so that contrast sliders cover a useful range instead of the full data type range (e.g. 0–65535).

Note: covered by the omero transitional metadata in OME-Zarr 0.6.
workaround: omero transitional metadata
notes: 0.5: Core extension (transitional omero metadata): `window` min/max.\n0.6: Core extension (transitional omero metadata): `omero` channels `window` min/max, separate from start/end.\n0.9dev: Core extension (was marked Transitional before the scale changed).

title: Lookup tables (colormaps)
statement: As a scientist visualizing intensity data,\nI want to say which lookup table or colormap a channel should use, and whether it’s inverted,\nso that images that depend on a specific colormap (e.g. heatmaps, inverted EM) display correctly everywhere, without relying on one server or application.
notes:
0.5: Only `omero` `inverted` and single `color`; no lookup tables.
0.6: Inversion is Transitional (`omero` `inverted`), and `color` gives a single-colour ramp, but there is no field for a lookup table or named colormap; that needs custom attributes.
0.9dev: `omero` has `inverted` and `color` but no lookup tables.
Forum (93505): asked for several lookup tables for the same image.

title: OME-XML sidecar file
statement:
As a data steward converting proprietary file formats to OME-Zarr,
I want a standard way to store a metadata.ome.xml file accessible from my Multiscale or Collection,
so I can preserve at least as much vendor metadata as when converting to OME-TIFF.

Note: currently doable in 0.6 with the bioformats2raw.layout transitional metadata.
workaround: bioformats2raw.layout transitional metadata
notes:
0.5: Core extension (transitional bioformats2raw.layout metadata) with `OME/METADATA.ome.xml`.
0.6: Core extension (transitional bioformats2raw.layout metadata): `bioformats2raw.layout` with `OME/METADATA.ome.xml`, but only for that layout, not for an arbitrary multiscale or collection.
0.9dev: Core extension (was marked Transitional before the scale changed).
Zurich 2026 links discussion: the bioformats2raw OME-XML is an implicit link; a general link type to single objects/files was discussed.
Forum (91705): Zarr and N5 do not allow arbitrary files in the hierarchy, so OME/METADATA.ome.xml is an extension (or breakage) of the container; the Fiji exporter does not write it.

title: OME-XML metadata as standardized JSON
statement:
As a maintainer of a tool that reads and writes OME-Zarr,
I want vendor metadata stored as standardized JSON fields,
so that I can preserve it without handling OME-XML.

Original: As a maintainer of a tool that reads/writes OME-Zarr,
I want a standard way to store the same metadata captured in a metadata.ome.xml file, but using only standardized fields in JSON (e.g. in zarr.json),
so I can preserve the vendor metadata without needing to know how to write/read/validate OME-XML and XML in general.
notes:
0.5: No standard JSON for OME-XML.
0.6: No standard JSON for OME-XML metadata in 0.6; only custom attributes.
Forum (44373): community metadata models (4DN-BINA-OME, QUAREP-LiMi) need one agreed, validatable representation in OME-Zarr.
Forum (111380): registering OME-Zarr on S3 in an image database (OMERO) without duplicating data currently relies on OME/METADATA.ome.xml, which may not exist; reading OME-Zarr metadata directly was asked for. EM metadata is also missing.
Forum (60885): 2022 call: OME metadata for full OMERO import may be large; chunking metadata was raised.

title: Photobleaching (FRAP) metadata
statement:
As a bioimage analyst doing FRAP microscopy,
I want to record when and where a photobleaching pulse occurred,
so that the data can be processed in standardized workflows.

Original: As a bioimage analyst doing FRAP microscopy,
I want to record the metadata for when the bleaching of the signal at a particular time with a lightsource. The properties of the photobleaching pulse (at least when and where it occurs) are relevant bits of metadata for this application. So I can seamlessly process the data in standardized workflows.
notes: 0.5: No acquisition or event metadata.\n0.6: No acquisition or event metadata in 0.6; custom attributes only.\n0.9dev: No acquisition or event metadata.

title: Basic axis names, units and scales
statement:
As a developer of microscope acquisition software,
I want to write axis names, units and scales with the image,
so that viewers such as ImageJ or Neuroglancer show correct axis names and scale bars.

Original: 1. Microscope interfacing software reads data from microscope and writes in ome-zarr format. Axis names and units are hard coded while the scales are set based on the imaging parameters.
2. User loads data in ImageJ/Neuroglancer and sees correct axis names and scale bars.
workaround: Feasible since 0.4 (axes + scale)
notes: 0.5: `axes` names, types, units and a `scale` per dataset.\n0.6: `axes` names, types and units plus a `scale` transform per dataset.\nForum (59298): asked that unit spellings such as um, micron, micrometre and µm be treated as equivalent.

title: Prediction on a cutout aligned to the full volume
statement:
As a bioimage analyst running a CNN on a cutout of a volume,
I want to save the prediction as a new image with a translation to the cutout location,
so that viewers show it aligned with the full original volume.

Original: 1. User runs CNN on cutout from existing volume in ome-zarr format and writes result as a new OME-Zarr volume, using a translation transformation to indicate the cutout location.
2. User loads CNN output and original volume in ImageJ/Neuroglancer and sees output correctly aligned to original full-size volume.
workaround: Feasible since 0.4 (translation)
notes: 0.5: A `translation` places the cutout in the volume's physical space.\n0.6: A `translation` (in the dataset or `scene` transforms) places the cutout in the full volume.\nForum (101906): annotate downloaded chunks offline and write them back with their spatial offset.

title: Affine registration between two volumes
statement:
As a bioimage analyst registering two volumes,
I want to store the affine transform in the metadata of the moving volume,
so that viewers show both volumes aligned without resampling.

Original: 1. User runs affine registration between existing volumes A and B in ome-zarr format. After computing affine transform, software modifies metadata of volume B in place to indicate the affine transform.
2. User loads data volumes A and B in Neuroglancer and sees them correctly aligned.
notes: 0.5: 0.5 has only scale and translation transforms; no affine.\n0.6: `affine` between the two images in a `scene`.

title: Non-rigid registration stored as a displacement field
statement:
As a bioimage analyst registering a volume to an atlas,
I want to store the non-rigid transform as a displacement field,
so that viewers show the volume, the atlas and segmentations of the volume aligned.

Original: 1. User performs non-rigid registration between existing volumes A (a canonical atlas) and B in ome-zarr format. BigWarp updates transformation meta-data in volume B, the non-rigid transformation is stored as a displacement field in ome-zarr format.
2. User loads data volumes A and B in BigDataViewer and sees them correctly aligned.
3. User overlays segmentations performed on original volume B (Story 2) and sees them correctly aligned.
notes: 0.5: 0.5 has only scale and translation transforms; no displacement fields.\n0.6: `displacements` transformation; overlaying segmentations from B works through B's labels.

title: Registration of slices into a volume
statement:
As a bioimage analyst with a series of slices,
I want to store each slice with transforms that place it in a common volume,
so that I can assemble the volume, or build it on the fly without saving it again.

Original: 1. User collects multiple overlapping/non-overlapping slices and stores each in ome-zarr format with appropriate transformations.
2. User collates all slices into a single ome-zarr volume (registering neighboring slices, joining the data, or introducing zeros/nans as necessary)
3. [Potential] User may want to simply save the transformations necessary to create the single volume on the fly.
notes: 0.5: 0.5 has only scale and translation transforms; slices needing rotation cannot be placed.\n0.6: Each slice as an image in a `scene` with its own transform. Collating them into one volume is up to tools, but the transforms are specified.\nZulip (Transformations in Java): an EM slice stack where each slice moves a little in xy.

title: Stitching overlapping tiles
statement:
As a bioimage analyst stitching overlapping tiles,
I want to store the transform from each tile to world space,
so that the stitched image can be displayed and processed from the original tiles.

Original: Related to story 5
1. User collects multiple overlapping 2d / 3d image tiles that are subsets of a whole.
2. User performs stitching (e.g., with BigStitcher), and needs to track transforms from all tile spaces to world space.
notes: 0.5: Translation-only stitching: each tile a separate image with its own translation in an implicit shared space. Rotations or overlap refinement out of spec.\n0.6: One transform per tile to a shared coordinate system in a `scene`.

title: Lens correction applied to every 2D slice
statement:
As a bioimage analyst,
I want to store a 2D lens distortion correction once and apply it to every slice of a 3D image,
so that the correction does not have to be duplicated per slice.

Original: 1. User working with an imaging system estimates its lens distortion as a non-linear 2D transform and stores it with NGFF.
2. User collects a 3D image.
3. User applies the same lens correction transform to all 2d slices of the 3D image.
notes: 0.5: 0.5 has only scale and translation transforms; no displacements or byDimension.\n0.6: `byDimension`: a 2D `displacements` field on y and x, identity on z.\nZulip (Fancy camera transforms): lens distortion models (as in the ROS camera spec) are not yet expressible.

title: Multiscale pyramids in a shared physical space
statement:
As a bioimage analyst with a large image,
I want to store a multiscale pyramid with the scale of each level,
so that viewers load levels on the fly and any two levels line up in the same physical space.

Original: 1. User has a large image stored at high resolution.

title: Correspondence of histology to MRI coordinates
statement:
As a neuroimaging researcher,
I want to register histology sections to an MRI volume with a chain of 2D and 3D transforms,
so that I can view each section next to the MRI and navigate between corresponding points.

Original: Related to 4, 5, 12 and 15, with details from the existing wb_view implementation
1. User collects T1w and other MRI scans of an animal, rigid aligns them and orients via ACPC or similar (not nonlinear or anisotropic affine)
2. Brain is extracted and sectioned, regularly spaced sections (whole brain, ~0.5mm in macaque) are stained, 2D scanned (and stitched) with full coverage (high resolution, image pyramids), with hemispheres and temporal pole pieces as separate images (due to FoV limits, separated tissue not being placed in correct relative position on the slide, bent corpus callosum misaligning hemispheres, etc)
3. Histology images are registered to MRI reference space, with the transform split into distinct parts.
   a. 2D to 2D affine for each piece to roughly position it within the section plane (for display without applying a deformation to image data)
   b. 2D to 2D deformation field (and its inverse) for each section to get accurate correspondence of histology tissue to the MRI tissue intersecting the section plane (tissue pliability, tearing, etc)
   c. 2D to 3D transform for each section to define the section plane in MRI mm space (currently affine, might include curvature in the future to deal with tissue deformation before sectioning)
4. For each image, a "distance beyond tissue edge" measurement is created for the tissue that the image is "responsible for", stored in rough aligned section plane space, used to resolve overlaps with background and/or clipped tissue when displaying all images from a section together.
5. User wants to display the histology image data one section at a time (all pieces in the section shown as per rough alignment), next to MRI data, and clicking on the histology moves the MRI display to the corresponding coordinate (and vice versa).
notes: 0.5: 0.5 has only scale and translation transforms; no affine, displacements or 2D-to-3D mapping.\n0.6: 2D `affine`, `displacements` with an explicit inverse (`bijection`) and a 2D-to-3D `affine` are all in 0.6; the distance map can be another image.

2. User performs drift correction, obtaining one (linear) transformation per timepoint.

Rigid or affine motion per timepoint has to be expanded into displacements.\n0.9dev: As 0.6: one shift per timepoint via a time-indexed `displacements` field; rigid/affine per timepoint must be expanded.

title: Registration of multiplexed imaging rounds

As a bioimage analyst doing multiplexed imaging,
I want to register several staining rounds via a shared marker and store only the transforms,

   a. first round: markers A, B, C.

As a bioimage analyst with 3D data,
I want to define a spline in 3D space,
so that I can process the data in a straightened space around it.

title: Mesh projection / surface quantification

As a bioimage analyst with a 3D image,
I want to define a surface mesh in it,
so that I can read or project image values onto the mesh.

Original: Motivates bounded (projective) coordinate spaces; intended for a follow-up transform RFC, not expected to be implemented in RFC-5
1. User has a 3D image.
2. User defines a 2D surface mesh in 3D space.
3. User gets image values at the mesh coordinates / projected to the mesh coordinates.
workaround: Not in RFC-5; intended for a follow-up transform RFC

title: CMI experiment as a graph of warped datasets
statement:
As a researcher doing correlative multimodal imaging,
I want to store the warps between datasets as a graph of landmark-based transforms,
so that data and annotations can be carried between any connected datasets without duplicating data.

Original: A correlative multimodal imaging experiment often involves multiple (>2) 3D datasets. A graph can be built such as: datasets are nodes; warp functions between any two datasets are edges linking these two nodes. A warp function (edge) between any two datasets can be defined by a set of parameters defining the origin and target datasets (e.g. dataset name, voxel size in metric units, offset, scale, axis flips) and a list of the coordinates of paired landmarks between these datasets. In this way, all edges and nodes can be listed in tables. The list of landmarks and warp functions can be sourced from BigWarp (and stored alongside the warp graph). This approach allows combining multiple warps in sequence (warping data across connected nodes in the graph). This approach not only allows warping the datasets themselves, but also the annotations drawn on any dataset. Any feature drawn on any dataset can be then overlaid onto any of the connected datasets seamlessly. Advantages:
1. Version control: the warp graph can be managed through git.
2. Scalability: more complex CMI workflows can be robustly built and shared efficiently across collaborators, e.g. a correlative light - XRay - EM workflow with multiple X-ray CT datasets obtained at different trimming stages.
3. Accuracy: by warping the annotations, any analysis can take place in the originally acquired datasets (instead of segmenting the warped datasets, which may have incorporated interpolation noise)
4. Cost-efficiency: packaging a CMI experiment only requires a single version of the original datasets (data-heavy) and the warp table (data-light); no dataset duplicates are needed.

This system has already been incorporated into an NGFF OME-Zarr data ecosystem (WEBKNOSSOS) as warpAnnotations, which facilitates multiuser collaboration and releasing CMI experiments.
notes: 0.5: No scene or non-scale/translation warps.\n0.6: The graph of datasets and warps maps onto a `scene` with transforms between images, and warps can be displacement fields. The landmarks behind each warp have no place in the spec.

title: Annotating and training with reference crops
statement:
As a bioimage analyst training segmentation models,
I want to save annotated reference crops as new images placed in the original volume,
so that I can train on the crops alone, including for data on an OMERO server.

Original: 1. User runs annotation tools (e.g. micro-sam) to segment reference crops (one or multiple); a reference crop is the same as the cut-outs in previous stories.
2. User writes the resulting annotated reference crop(s) in a new OME-Zarr volume (following Story 2).
   a. An interesting use-case would be to do the above two steps for data on an OMERO server (and ensure that the user does not have to create a zero array locally to do step 2)
3. User wants to train models on segmented reference crops only.
notes: 0.5: The crop can be its own image with a `translation` into the full image's physical space (implicit; no scene). Not as a label image, which must match the image shape.\n0.6: The annotated crop can be its own image placed with a `translation` in a `scene`, so no zero-filled full-size array is needed. Label images under `labels` must match the image shape, so a crop is not a label image there.\nForum (37948): collaborators annotate for training; exports differ by crop, resolution and label mapping.
