title: Subject-local orientation of tissue specimens
statement:
As a researcher in spatial transcriptomics or histopathology,
I want to record a specimen's own orientation (e.g. superficial-to-deep),
so that it can be analysed without registering to a whole-body atlas.

Original: As a researcher in spatial transcriptomics or histopathology, I want to record the orientation of a tissue specimen itself (e.g. superficial-to-deep in a skin biopsy, apical-to-basal in an epithelium) even when its place in the donor is unknown, so that it can be analysed without registering to a whole-body atlas.
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: custom attributes only.\n0.6: Out of spec: same as 0.5.\n0.9dev: Core: RFC-4 subject-local values (superficial/deep, apical/basal, apex/base). Only one primary orientation per axis.

title: Standalone label images
statement: As a bioimage analyst or data manager,\nI want to store a label image (segmentation) as its own OME-Zarr fileset, without a parent intensity image or a labels/ group,\nso that segmentations can be shared and loaded on their own, as already done in practice (e.g. BIA AI-ready studies).
user_classes: Bioimage analyst; Data manager; Tool developer
workaround: Write a multiscales group at the root with the image-label key; readers that only check multiscales open it as a plain image.
notes:
0.5: Possible: a multiscales group with image-label works and is used, but the spec only describes labels nested under an image's labels/ group, so it is not clearly allowed.
0.6: Possible: same; a scene can also hold the image and its label side by side, with image-label marking the label.
0.9dev: Possible: unchanged; done when the text says a single image with image-label is valid. A labels RFC is expected.
Forum (123114): example: BIA AI gallery images with separate linked label OME-Zarrs.
sources: https://github.com/ome/ngff/issues/179 duplicate; https://github.com/ome/ngff/issues/536 labels epic; https://forum.image.sc/t/ome-zarr-hackathon-how-to-represent-labels/123114/9 labels RFC discussion; https://github.com/ome/ngff/issues/339; https://github.com/ome/ngff/issues/338; https://forum.image.sc/t/how-to-recognize-a-labelimage-stored-in-a-file/58526; https://forum.image.sc/t/save-a-single-labels-dataset-into-an-ome-zarr/93505

title: Several images shown together in one view
statement: As a researcher using viewers such as WEBKNOSSOS, Neuroglancer, MoBIE or OMERO.figure,\nI want to describe several images that map to a common space as one entity,\nso that I can share one link instead of many and every viewer opens the same set.
workaround: Viewer-specific JSON (MoBIE projects, Neuroglancer state) listing the images.
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no way to group images; viewer-specific JSON only.
0.6: Core: an RFC-5 scene groups images in shared coordinate systems. Rendering settings are a separate story.
0.9dev: Core: same; RFC-8 would generalise scenes into collections.
Forum (47400): example: overview image with embedded high-magnification regions browsed like a map (CLEM, petapixel-style).
Forum (122592): OMERO.figure saved as an RFC-8 collection referring to existing remote arrays by URL.

title: Segmentations and prediction maps related to several images
statement: As a bioimage analyst,\nI want a label image or prediction map to refer to several images (m:n), e.g. correlated images of the same feature or channels stored as separate images,\nso that derived images are not tied to a single parent.
workaround: Duplicate the labels under each image, or record the links in custom attributes.
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: labels are 1:n under one image; prediction maps have no defined kind.\n0.6: Out of spec: same; a scene can place them side by side but not say which image a label belongs to.\n0.9dev: Out of spec: not in 0.9dev; RFC-8 collections would cover it.

title: Workflow outputs that link to unchanged inputs
statement: As a tool developer of a workflow engine (Fractal, Voxelytics, Nextflow),\nI want a task to write its output (e.g. a prediction map) in a new fileset that links to the input image without copying it,\nso that inputs stay untouched and each task's output can be viewed with its input.
workaround: Copy the input, or write into the input fileset, or record the path in custom attributes.
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: no links to images outside the fileset.\n0.6: Out of spec: scenes reference images inside their own hierarchy only.\n0.9dev: Out of spec: not in 0.9dev; RFC-8 collections would cover it.

title: Flexible metadata for plates and wells
statement: As a data producer of high content screens,\nI want to say how images in a well relate (field of view, re-acquisition, processed result), and describe wells of different sizes or positions,\nso that viewers pick sensible defaults and plates can hold processing intermediates.
workaround: Custom attributes on the plate or well group.
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: the HCS plate/well metadata has a fixed set of fields.
0.6: Out of spec: same.
0.9dev: Out of spec: not in 0.9dev; RFC-8 collections would cover it.
Zulip (High-content screening spec vs single zarr array): HCS producers want arbitrary per-field metadata (ground truth, partitions such as train/test, cell type) that loads fast; some store it in binary arrays because large JSON parses slowly.

title: Image collections for archive deposition and access
statement: As a data manager at an image archive,\nI want submitters to group images and say how they relate (same acquisition series, plate/well), and to publish groupings that viewers understand,\nso that submissions can be parsed into records and data opens in many tools without a schema per tool.
workaround: Plates for HCS; otherwise archive-specific manifests.
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: only plates group images.
0.6: Possible: scenes group spatially related images, but say nothing about other relations.
0.9dev: Possible: not in 0.9dev; RFC-8 collections would cover it.
Forum (71330): several light-sheet tiles per session; top-level metadata also needed to detect incomplete uploads.

title: Viewer rendering state stored with a collection
statement: As a researcher sharing a multi-image view,\nI want to store the view state (position, rotation, per-layer colours, shaders, visibility) alongside the images, in viewer-specific containers,\nso that others open the same view.
workaround: Viewer-specific state files or URLs.
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: omero rendering covers one image's channels only.
0.6: Out of spec: same.
0.9dev: Out of spec: not in 0.9dev; RFC-8 collections would cover it. RFC-8 gives containers, not a rendering spec.
Forum (85537): several saved views (regions, channels, rendering mode) per dataset.
Forum (123099): view settings should record where and how a figure view was made and can give archives a thumbnail; channel visibility and layer order still missing.
Forum (55333): 3D Slicer also wants colormaps, surface and volume rendering presets stored with the data.

title: Linking tables, meshes and other derived data to images
statement: As a bioimage analyst,\nI want to link derived data (tables, meshes, probability maps) in Zarr or other formats to an OME-Zarr image,\nso that tools can discover it without each defining its own sub-spec.
workaround: Tool-specific conventions, e.g. ngio tables (Fractal) or MoBIE label tables.
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: only labels are defined.
0.6: Out of spec: same.
0.9dev: Out of spec: not in 0.9dev; RFC-8 collections would cover it.
Forum (123109): Zurich 2026 SpatialData track: store points, shapes and tables next to images, possibly as an RFC-8 extension or Zarr convention.
Forum (55333): an analyst keeps image, label properties, labels and cell population definitions (CSV) in separate files and wants them in one Zarr.
Zulip (tables): table row/column APIs for MoBIE/BDV mirroring AnnData.

title: Gallery and grid views
statement: As a researcher,\nI want to show many similar images (each possibly with its labels) as a grid of thumbnails from their lowest resolution,\nso that I get an overview and can zoom into the interesting ones.
workaround: Tool-specific tables, e.g. MoBIE collection tables, Zarrcade, BioFile Finder.
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no gallery grouping; plates only for wells.
0.6: Out of spec: scenes place images in space, not as a grid.
0.9dev: Out of spec: not in 0.9dev; RFC-8 collections would cover it.
Forum (123100): CSV tables of OME-Zarr URLs are used as collections by BFF, MoBIE, zarrcade and the IDR samples page.
examples: https://github.com/normanrz/ngff-rfc8-collection-examples/ RFC-8 examples incl. OpenOrganelle mito gallery

title: View and analyse stitched data without a fused copy
statement: As a facility or analyst handling large tiled acquisitions,\nI want viewers and analysis libraries to fuse tiles on demand from the raw tiles and their registration transforms,\nso that I need not store a fused copy (roughly doubling storage) or pay to compute fusion for regions nobody looks at.
user_classes: Data manager; Bioimage analyst; Tool developer
workaround: Write the fused image anyway.
notes:
0.5: Possible: translation-only tiles as separate images in an implicit shared space.
0.6: Core: a scene holds every tile and its transform to a shared space, which is all a reader needs to fuse; doing it fast for many tiles is STORY-073.
0.9dev: Core: same.
Forum (119093): ZEISS: microscopists need access to the acquisition tiles, not only a fused image.
Zulip (OME-ZARR and overlapping tiles): raw, pre-aligned tiles kept unfused, as in Render.

title: Find which tiles cover a region
statement: As a viewer developer,\nI want a world-to-tile lookup (spatial index) for collections of thousands of tiles,\nso that rendering a region does not require reading every tile's metadata, one request per node, on remote storage.
workaround: Read all tile metadata up front, or a tool-specific index.
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no index.
0.6: Out of spec: readers must scan every transform in the scene.
0.9dev: Out of spec: RFC-8 does not define one; its extensions could carry one, or consolidated metadata.
Zulip (OME-ZARR and overlapping tiles): for millions of tiles it matters whether metadata maps tile-to-world or world-to-tile.

title: Provenance of registration and fusion
statement: As a researcher,\nI want a registration stored as its own result that references the raw tiles and records how it was produced (tool, parameters),\nso that I can reproduce or audit how a fused image was made.
workaround: Tool logs or custom attributes.
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: nowhere to record it.\n0.6: Out of spec: a scene holds the transforms, but there is no provenance field.\n0.9dev: Out of spec: RFC-8 gives attributes and source references but no provenance schema.

title: Select a channel by name
statement: As a bioimage analyst running batch analysis on many multi-channel images,\nI want to look up a channel's index from a stable name (e.g. "nuclei"),\nso my pipeline finds the right channel even when channel order differs between datasets.
workaround: omero.channels[].label
notes:
0.5: Core extension: transitional omero.channels[].label names each channel, but labels are not required to be unique or stable identifiers.
0.6: Core extension: unchanged; omero still transitional.
0.9dev: Core extension: ome/ngff-spec#87 makes some omero fields optional; RFC-7 is expected to give channels proper identifiers.
Workarounds seen in the wild: omero.channels label, or even channel color, used as identifier. CF conventions handle this with a labels/auxiliary coordinate array along the axis (d-v-b).
Forum (97798): asked how to address a single channel in a URL (e.g. `my.ome.zarr;ch=0`).

title: High-content screening plate layout
statement: As a screening facility,\nI want to store a plate as wells and fields of view (with plate acquisitions), each field a multiscale image,\nso viewers and analysis tools can navigate and load sparse plates by well and field.
notes:
0.5: Core: plate/well metadata (HCS spec since 0.1.4).
0.6: Core: unchanged; acquisitions, rowIndex/columnIndex, field_count.
0.9dev: Core: unchanged.
Defined in the HCS spec (plate/well metadata) since 0.1-0.4; record of the original need.

title: Segmentations stored with the image
statement: As a bioimage analyst,\nI want to store one or more multiscale integer label images (segmentations) inside the image they segment,\nso viewers discover and overlay them without extra configuration.
notes:
0.5: Core: labels group with image-label multiscales (since 0.1.3).
0.6: Core: unchanged; labels can be linked with identity/scale/translation transforms.
0.9dev: Core: unchanged.
Basis of the labels spec since 0.1.
Zurich 2026 links discussion: `image-label` `source.image` points to a group, not saying which of its multiscales is meant.
Forum (75907): the parent image says nothing about whether a labels/ group exists, so tools must probe for it.
Forum (97327): in an IDR plate one row has no labels; tools (MoBIE) had assumed all images in a plate have labels or none.
Forum (72244): segmentations are often computed at lower resolution than the raw, so label levels start at a coarser scale than the image; WEBKNOSSOS and MoBIE kept segmentations outside labels/ as too inflexible.
Zulip (OME-NGFF: images and downsampled labels): an archive submission had segmentations at lower resolution than the multiplexed image; scale metadata avoids upsampling the labels, but tools need real examples.
Zulip (what does "two datasets" mean for image-label metadata?): the rule that labels have as many levels as the image is unclear and blocks labels made at a larger voxel size.
Zulip (Reading only one dataset from on OME-Zarr): a URL to an image that has labels/ does not say whether to open only the image or the labels too.

title: Downsampling factors of pyramid levels
statement: As a tool developer (e.g. BigDataViewer),\nI want each resolution level to declare how it was downsampled relative to the full resolution, including when only some axes (e.g. not z) are downsampled,\nso I do not have to infer factors from array shapes, which fails when extents are not divisible.
workaround: Divide per-level scale by level-0 scale
notes:
0.5: Possible: per-level scale transforms give the factors by division; multiscales type/metadata describe the method. No dedicated field.
0.6: Possible: same; spec now says scale MUST express the factor when no physical size applies.
0.9dev: Possible: unchanged.
Since 0.4 per-level scale transforms make this derivable; d-v-b argued tools should use grid spacing instead.
Forum (37930): downsample factors that differ per dimension, raised when multiscales v0.1 was proposed.
Forum (48386): 2021 call: serial-section EM downsamples in xy until isotropic, then in all axes.
Zulip (Scale naming for upscales): pyramids that include upsampled levels above the acquired resolution; nothing marks which level is the acquired one.

title: Volumes with millions of chunks on a file system
statement: As a user storing large volumes on local or network file systems,\nI want chunks laid out in nested directories rather than one flat folder,\nso the file system copes with millions of chunks.
notes:
0.5: Core: Zarr v3 chunk key encoding ("/" separator) nests chunks (since 0.2 for v2).
0.6: Core: unchanged.
0.9dev: Core: unchanged.
Addressed at Zarr level (dimension_separator, then Zarr v3 chunk key encoding).
Forum (48386): 2021 call: sysadmins report 845M files in 252 TB on one file system.

title: Meshes stored with images
statement: As a bioimage analyst producing surface reconstructions,\nI want to store meshes (vertices, faces, properties) next to the images they come from,\nso meshes and images can be shared and viewed together.
workaround: Neuroglancer precomputed meshes or side files
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no mesh storage.
0.6: Out of spec: no mesh storage.
0.9dev: Out of spec: mesh RFC in draft (kephale).
Proposal based on PLY; glyg suggested GeoJSON for ROIs/points instead.
Forum (110810): multiscale mesh example for RFC-8.
Zulip (Meshes in NGFF): users who mesh label images want to pack the meshes into the Zarr, with Neuroglancer precomputed as a reference.

title: Vector shapes and annotations
statement: As a image annotator,\nI want to store polygons, polylines, lines, ellipses and points in image coordinates,\nso viewers like vizarr and napari can display and exchange my annotations.
workaround: GeoJSON side files
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no shapes.
0.6: Out of spec: no shapes.
0.9dev: Out of spec: no shapes.
GeoJSON vs WKT discussed; neither has ellipses/rectangles or nD.
Forum (111042): annotations stored with remote cloud images and kept in sync across users (QuPath).
Forum (72839): points and regions from whole-slide annotation files, overlaid when viewing a region.
Forum (84282): polygon and centre-of-mass annotations outlining structures in image stacks.
Forum (55333): 3D Slicer wants markups (lines, angles, point sets, curves, boxes) alongside images, segmentations, meshes and tables in one interoperable format.
Forum (123086): Zarr Vectors: multiscale points, meshes, skeletons and networks stored as Zarr groups next to images.
Forum (48386): 2021 call: cryo-EM needs particle positions with orientations and links (e.g. to PDB).
Forum (48348): QuPath and Orbit converged on GeoJSON for exchanging annotations.
Forum (37948): annotation exchange for training data: vector, label image or multichannel binary, each with many choices.
Forum (95914): no common annotation format across HALO, Visiopharm and QuPath.
Zulip (GeoJSON or something else for ROIs): serialising polygon ROIs from Java; GeoParquet suggested for up to 1B points and 100M polygons; one framework keeps vector data outside Zarr.

title: Regions of interest
statement: As a analyst processing fields of view or organoids within a large dataset,\nI want to define regions of interest (e.g. bounding boxes in physical units) on an image,\nso processing and viewing can target those regions without copying data.
workaround: ROI tables (Fractal) or separate cropped images
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no ROI or table spec.
0.6: Out of spec: a crop can be stored as its own image placed with a translation in a scene, but a region without copying data has no place.
0.9dev: Out of spec: unchanged.
Options: ROI tables (Fractal; preferred by bogovicj) vs crops in transformations (MoBIE).
Zulip (High-content screening spec vs single zarr array): ROI tables (physical bounding boxes, optional label mask) are stored instead of crops.

title: Units and meaning of image values
statement: As a scientist storing quantitative images (FLIM lifetimes, calcium dF/F, AFM height),\nI want to record the physical unit and kind (continuous, categorical) of the stored values, even per channel,\nso the values can be interpreted and processed correctly.
workaround: Custom attributes; Zarr unit convention (zarr-convention-uom)
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: units only for axes, not for values.
0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.
0.9dev: Out of spec: unchanged.
#37 asks about channels whose values have different units (compound datasets). Zarr convention for units: clbarnes/zarr-convention-uom.
Forum (123114): Zurich 2026 labels discussion: labels as images with categorical values; AFM height maps (and industrial height-map channels) need value type and unit.
Forum (110810): a Zarr units-of-measure convention (UCUM) for array values was proposed.
Zulip (Axes units): units for intensities wanted alongside axis units.

title: Interoperability with xarray and CF conventions
statement: As a developer working across geoscience and bioimaging tools,\nI want OME-Zarr images to be readable as xarray datasets with explicit coordinates and CF-style metadata,\nso domain-agnostic tools can use bioimages and we reuse mature conventions.
notes:
0.5: Possible: Zarr v3 dimension_names (MUST since 0.5.2) lets xarray open each array with named dims, but without coordinates or CF attributes.
0.6: Possible: same; coordinates transforms give explicit per-sample coordinates, but as multiscale groups xarray does not read.
0.9dev: Unsure: RFC-3 lifts axis restrictions, closer to xarray; no CF mapping defined.
Zulip (potential RFC: coordinate arrays): several coordinate variables on one axis (timepoints plus a label per timepoint), as in xarray.

title: Per-label names and display properties
statement: As a medical/bioimage tool developer (e.g. 3D Slicer),\nI want each label value to carry a name, standard term, color, opacity and custom properties in one consistent structure,\nso others can tell what each labeled object represents.
notes:
0.5: Core: image-label colors (rgba) and properties with arbitrary keys per label-value.
0.6: Core: unchanged.
0.9dev: Core: unchanged; colors/properties split (ngff#79) still open; labels RFC expected.
#164: user cannot tell what IDR labels represent when names are missing.
Forum (43483): a table with one row per label and columns of label attributes was asked for in the first labels proposal.
Forum (74459): in IDR sample labels there is no way to know what each labelled object represents.
Forum (48386): 2021 call: label values mapped through a lookup table (largest dtype plus mapping) allow fast relabelling without rewriting voxels.
Forum (32923): labels carry tags and colours, possibly different per timepoint.
Forum (47618): finding one object in a huge label image needs per-label pointers such as bounding boxes.

title: Pixel origin at center or corner
statement: As a developer exchanging images between 2D and 3D tools (ITK, VTK, napari),\nI want the spec to define whether coordinates refer to pixel centers or corners,\nso images and annotations align across tools without half-pixel shifts.
notes:
0.5: Unsure: check whether the 0.5 text defines the pixel origin; the explicit "Coordinate convention" section came with RFC-5.
0.6: Core: "The pixel/voxel center is the origin of the continuous coordinate system"; pixel = half-open box [-0.5, 0.5).
0.9dev: Core: unchanged.
Pixel-center convention adopted; #492 asks to define "pixel" consistently.

title: Fast plate overview
statement: As a viewer developer (vizarr, napari),\nI want a precomputed low-resolution overview of a whole plate,\nso opening a 384-well plate does not take thousands of requests.
workaround: Viewers load the lowest level of every well
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no plate-level preview.
0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.
0.9dev: Out of spec: unchanged.
Zulip (High-content screening spec vs single zarr array): a viewer keeps HCS metadata in a few top-level JSON files to render thousands of images from S3.

title: Millions of spots from spatial omics
statement: As a spatial-omics analyst,\nI want to store millions of detected spots (2D/3D coordinates, gene name, quality) with the image,\nso they can be loaded chunk-wise, locally or from object storage.
workaround: Parquet / AnnData (SpatialData) next to the image
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no points or tables.
0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.
0.9dev: Out of spec: unchanged.
d-v-b: zarr arrays are a poor fit for tables; consider parquet etc.
Forum (57337): 2021 spatial omics hackathon: also SMLM localisations, spots per tile and round, with efficient spatial access.
Forum (61393): single-molecule localisation data (STORM, PALM, PAINT, MERFISH) stored as point clouds instead of rendered rasters.
Forum (57400): SMLM viewers need multi-resolution point structures (octrees, as in Potree/Entwine) for instant display of billions of localisations.

title: Single-resolution images
statement: As a analyst extracting a small region from one scale level,\nI want to save a single-resolution image with axes and transforms without multiscale boilerplate,\nso small derived images stay simple yet valid.
workaround: Multiscales with one dataset
notes:
0.5: Possible: a multiscales group with one level is valid, if verbose.
0.6: Possible: same; one level still needs coordinateSystems and a transform.
0.9dev: Possible: unchanged; RFC-8 proposes a singlescale node.
RFC-8 proposes a singlescale node.
Forum (123104): Zurich 2026 hackathon: needs are tens of thousands of small images, small timepoints and intermediate results; a single-level multiscale doubles the metadata files. Upgrading a singlescale to a multiscale later without rewriting was raised as a requirement.

title: Description, license and authorship
statement: As a data producer sharing an image,\nI want to store a free-text description, license, authors and contributions with the image,\nso reuse terms and credit travel with the data.
workaround: Custom attributes; OME-XML via bioformats2raw for some fields
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no description, license or author fields.
0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.
0.9dev: Out of spec: unchanged.
Forum (85537): sharing a small volume via Zenodo/Figshare needed free text, authorship and license.
Forum (110810): a Zarr license convention (SPDX) was proposed.
Forum (41136): IDR data is CC-BY but the licence was not in the Zarr metadata.
Zulip (License statements in OME-Zarr files & copyright liabilities): a structured license field is wanted by archives serving CC-BY data; options discussed: schema.org/RO-Crate terms, a Zarr license convention, or a referenced license file.
ngff#213 (2025–2026): an RO-Crate sidecar was suggested as an alternative that leaves zarr.json untouched; a 'bibliography' block (name, description, tags, CURIEs, DOIs to cite, license URL) was proposed, delegating authorship to DOI records; the counter-view is to vendor the metadata through Zarr-level conventions (CITATION.cff, CSL-JSON, SPDX licenses) rather than rely on third-party services; parked until RFC-8 extensions settle.

title: Sparse arrays
statement: As a user of mask images or mass spectrometry imaging with thousands of channels,\nI want to store mostly-empty data as sparse arrays,\nso storage and computation scale with content, not volume.
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: dense arrays only; needs Zarr-level sparse support (zarr-specs#245).
0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.
0.9dev: Out of spec: unchanged.
Maintainers point to Zarr-level support (zarr-specs#245).
Zulip (Adaptive Pixel Representation (APR)): adaptive (non-grid) pixel representations want to follow the multiscale and metadata conventions.

title: Several image types per HCS field of view
statement: As a developer of an optical pooled screening pipeline,\nI want each field of view in a plate to hold the raw image, float derived images and segmentations together,\nso co-registered outputs with different dtypes stay organized in the HCS layout.
workaround: Sibling plates for derived images; labels for integer masks
notes:
0.5: Awkward: well images must be multiscales images; float derived images fit only as separate plates or extra fields of view.
0.6: Awkward: a scene can group co-registered images, but a well field must be a multiscales image, so scenes cannot sit in wells (ngff#476).
0.9dev: Awkward: unchanged.
#476 proposes nesting scenes in HCS.

title: Unique identifiers for images
statement: As a curator cataloguing many OME-Zarr datasets,\nI want each image to carry a stable unique identifier,\nso copies and derived versions can be tracked across stores.
workaround: Custom attributes
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no identifier field.
0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.
0.9dev: Out of spec: unchanged.
Problem statement still debated (d-v-b, mkitti).
Forum (110810): BIO-CODES explores similarity-preserving ISCC fingerprints for OME-Zarr.
Zulip (Table spec proposal #64): images need unique IDs, or many images named 1.ome.zarr will sit on the cloud.

title: JPEG-compressed RGB images
statement: As a data producer converting brightfield whole-slide images,\nI want to store RGB images with the Zarr JPEG codec,\nso files stay as small as the vendor originals and viewers decode chunks with standard JPEG libraries.
workaround: Store (c, y, x) and add a transpose codec [1, 2, 0] before the jpeg codec so chunks are encoded channel-last
notes:
0.5: Awkward: JPEG needs interleaved channel-last chunks, but axes must put channel before space; only works through a transpose codec.
0.6: Awkward: same axis-order rule.
0.9dev: Awkward: RFC-3 lifts the ordering rule, so (y, x, c) arrays may be allowed; kept Awkward until checked with readers.
The Zarr jpeg codec spec is minimal by design; lossless/16-bit JPEG would need separate codecs. Readers with support: ome-zarr-py + zarr-ext-jpeg, Fiji, neuroglancer, vizarr; zarrita.js PR; imagecodecs 2026.11.11 JpegCodec. No conformance test suite yet.

title: Reuse vendor JPEG tiles without re-encoding
statement: As a data producer converting NDPI/SVS/TIFF/DICOM slides,\nI want to copy their existing JPEG tiles into OME-Zarr chunks as they are,\nso conversion is fast and adds no extra compression loss.
workaround: Bio-Formats extracts NDPI tiles as chunks; imagecodecs jpeg_merge/jpeg_transcode rebuild or retile JPEG streams losslessly
notes:
0.5: Awkward: same channel-last constraint as STORY-094 (transpose codec); vendor tile sizes give small chunks, so sharding is needed for performance.
0.6: Awkward: unchanged.
0.9dev: Awkward: unchanged for now.
Forum (123102): JPEG 2000 files carry their own wavelet pyramid; refkv exposes it as OME-Zarr levels without re-encoding.
Zulip (Rechunk jpeg-based formats into zarr): converting NDPI to Zarr inflates data about 10x; reusing the JPEG strips losslessly as chunks, or a virtual store over the original, is preferred.

title: Expansion microscopy: microscope and specimen scale
statement: As a data producer imaging expanded specimens,\nI want to store the voxel size reported by the microscope and the expansion factor (and how it was measured) separately,\nso viewers show the image at pre-expansion specimen size while the acquisition resolution stays recoverable.
workaround: Microscope voxel size as per-level scale; inverse expansion factor (1/f) as multiscales-level scale; measurement method in custom attributes. EM volumes use [1, 1, 1].
notes:
0.5: Awkward: the expansion factor has to be bent into a multiscales-level scale with no named spaces; the two scales compose to specimen size, but there is no field saying the outer scale is an expansion factor, and nothing for how it was measured.
0.6: Possible: named coordinate systems (e.g. "microscope" and "specimen") with a scale between them make the two spaces explicit; the measurement method still needs custom metadata.
0.9dev: Possible: unchanged.
Convention used by AI-HHMI/miao on internal datasets; ome/ngff#565 proposes documenting modality conventions.
Forum (122243): multiscale-level scale used today to separate microscope scale from expansion factor.

title: Stream images from object storage without a server
statement: As a data manager publishing reference datasets (e.g. IDR),\nI want images stored so any tool can read individual chunks directly over HTTP or S3,\nso users view and analyse multi-TB data without downloading it or running an image server.
notes:
0.5: Core: chunked Zarr arrays readable over HTTP/S3.
0.6: Core: unchanged.
0.9dev: Core: unchanged.
Motivating use case of the 2021 paper (latency benchmark: Zarr ~10x faster than HDF5/TIFF on cloud storage).

title: Multiresolution pyramids for interactive viewing
statement: As a researcher browsing large images,\nI want lower-resolution copies stored alongside the full-resolution image,\nso viewers show an overview at once and load detail only where I zoom.
notes: 0.5: Core: multiscales datasets ordered highest to lowest resolution.\n0.6: Core: unchanged, per-level scale/translation into the intrinsic coordinate system.\n0.9dev: Core: unchanged.

title: Parallel writing during conversion
statement: As a data producer converting large proprietary files,\nI want many processes to write different parts of an image at the same time,\nso conversion of TB-scale data finishes in reasonable time.
notes: 0.5: Core: chunks are independent objects; bioformats2raw writes them in parallel. Writes into one shard need coordination.\n0.6: Core: unchanged.\n0.9dev: Core: unchanged.

title: Fewer files for copying and archiving
statement: As a data manager moving datasets between storage systems,\nI want small chunks grouped into fewer, larger files,\nso copying millions of chunk files does not take far longer than one large file.
notes:
0.5: Core: Zarr v3 sharding codec is allowed ("all features of the Zarr format ... MAY be used").
0.6: Core: unchanged.
0.9dev: Core: unchanged.
The 2021 paper names file count as the main downside of NGFF (4.3 million files for a 264 GB LSM dataset; S3 upload fell from >100 to <20 MiB/s).
Zulip (OME-Zarr: status of sharding support): missing sharding was seen as a roadblock to adoption (2022); sharded writes from dask arrived in 2025.

title: Upgrade data to newer spec versions
statement: As a data manager holding years of published OME-Zarr data,\nI want to migrate datasets to newer spec versions with tools, without rewriting pixel data,\nso old data stays readable without maintaining old readers forever.
workaround: Rewrite only the zarr.json metadata; 0.4 to 0.5 also needs Zarr v2 to v3 metadata conversion
notes:
0.5: Possible: ome.version marks the version, so tools can detect and upgrade; no migration rules in the spec.
0.6: Possible: unchanged; the changelog lists breaking changes per version.
0.9dev: Possible: unchanged.
Forum (123106): RFC-8 plans a legacy multiscale node so unchanged 0.5/0.6 images stay valid.
Forum (110810): how much 0.3/0.4 data still exists is unknown; BIA and CryoET Data Portal still write 0.4.
Zulip (in-place conversion of ome-zarr v0.4 to v0.5): converting 0.4 to 0.5 by rewriting metadata only and keeping chunks.

title: Same metadata in OME-TIFF, HDF5 and Zarr
statement: As a data producer choosing a container per use (TIFF for pathology tools, HDF5 for local, Zarr for cloud),\nI want one metadata model shared by all three,\nso converting between them loses nothing.
workaround: OME-XML in OME-TIFF and in OME/METADATA.ome.xml (bioformats2raw)
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: OME-Zarr metadata is Zarr-specific; only the transitional bioformats2raw layout carries OME-XML.
0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.
0.9dev: Out of spec: unchanged.
Example: an ICC profile in a source TIFF is lost on conversion to OME-Zarr (STORY-123).
Forum (84840): a DICOM WSI bridge was asked for clinical interoperability.

title: Versioning of data and metadata
statement: As a data manager of a public archive (e.g. DANDI),\nI want changes to pixel data and metadata recorded as versions,\nso analyses can cite exactly the version they used and earlier versions stay reachable.
workaround: Versioned S3 buckets plus DataLad datasets (DANDI); Zarr-level stores such as Icechunk
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no versioning in OME-Zarr or Zarr v3.
0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.
0.9dev: Out of spec: unchanged.
Named as a specification under consideration in the 2023 paper.
Forum (60885): 2022 call: versioning metadata when a transformation changes (e.g. after re-registration).

title: Serve existing files as OME-Zarr without converting
statement: As a data manager of a petabyte-scale archive (e.g. Brain Image Library),\nI want existing TIFF/HDF5/other files exposed as OME-Zarr on the fly,\nso OME-Zarr tools can read them without duplicating the data.
workaround: kerchunk reference files; server-side microservices that translate chunk requests (BrAinPI)
notes:
0.5: Possible: the spec is storage-agnostic, so a service or reference store presenting valid zarr.json and chunks is valid OME-Zarr; nothing in the spec covers it.
0.6: Possible: unchanged.
0.9dev: Possible: unchanged.
Forum (123103): Fileglancer: most data on institutional storage will never be converted, since converting doubles storage.
Forum (123077): napari-virtual-reader shows CZI/TIFF as virtual OME-Zarr; its .vzip reference archive is not self-contained and needs the source file unchanged.
Forum (123098): static (references into existing files) and dynamic (computed chunks) virtualization were both explored.
Zulip (Rechunk jpeg-based formats into zarr): a JPEG-aware store could expose NDPI/SVS as Zarr without intermediate files.

title: Write OME-Zarr directly from acquisition software
statement: As a microscope developer (e.g. ImSwitch),\nI want acquisition software to write OME-Zarr with its experiment metadata as data is acquired,\nso no conversion step is needed and data is ready for distributed processing at once.
workaround: ome-zarr-py writer from the control software
notes:
0.5: Possible: any writer can produce OME-Zarr; arrays can be resized as timepoints arrive, but nothing marks a dataset as still being written and acquisition metadata has no standard place.
0.6: Possible: unchanged.
0.9dev: Possible: unchanged.
Forum (66794): Micro-Manager and light-sheet groups stream at up to 4 GB/s, often with the number of timepoints unknown until the end; one file per plane is too slow.
Forum (123075): Fiji can now reload a growing OME-Zarr during acquisition, but only pixels are re-read, not metadata.
Forum (48386): 2021 call: cameras stream one image at a time and will not write 64^3 chunks; data may need rechunking after acquisition.
Zulip (extending an existing array with ome-zarr-py): appending a timepoint to an existing image means resizing every level and updating metadata; tools do not support it.
Zulip (reading Zarr that is being written in Java): viewers following an acquisition must re-check chunks not yet written; caches treat missing chunks as empty.

title: Single-file OME-Zarr
statement: As a researcher with small or local datasets,\nI want an OME-Zarr stored as one file (a ZIP),\nso I can email, upload and drag-and-drop it into desktop tools like any other image file.
workaround: Uncompressed ZIP64 with the Zarr root at the ZIP root, following the RFC-9 draft; read via ZipStore (zarr-python, zarrita.js, zarrs, Zarr.jl)
notes:
0.5: Possible: a zipped store is valid Zarr, but neither spec says how to package or detect it, and Java/R readers lacked support.
0.6: Possible: unchanged.
0.9dev: Possible: not yet in the spec; RFC-9 (Zipped OME-Zarr, .ozx) is at R4, replying to reviews. Once adopted this becomes Core.
Hackathon recommendations: ZIP over other archives (central directory helps HTTP range reads); writers make uncompressed ZIP64; readers may accept compressed ZIPs.
RFC-9 requires the ZIP root to be the OME-Zarr root, no nesting in another OME-Zarr and no multi-part archives; recommends ZIP64, no ZIP compression, sharding, zarr.json entries first (breadth-first), an archive comment {"ome": {"version": …}} with optional zipFile.centralDirectory.jsonFirst, and the .ozx extension. Validation kit: ozx-tck.

title: Processing tasks that add results to an existing OME-Zarr
statement: As a workflow developer (Fractal, Nextflow, Snakemake, napari),\nI want each task to take an OME-Zarr location, write its labels or tables back into it, and declare what it added,\nso the same task runs unchanged in any workflow engine and the next step can find its output.
workaround: Fractal task manifests (JSON schema for inputs; outputs only partly described)
notes:
0.5: Possible: labels can be added under labels/, but there is no standard place for tables and nothing records which task added what.
0.6: Possible: unchanged.
0.9dev: Possible: unchanged; RFC-8 collections may give derived data a place.
Open points from the hackathon: output metadata schema, writing subsets (timepoints, channels, ROIs) from parallel processes.
Zulip (Is there a tool that I can incrementally save data.): saving network predictions as each timepoint finishes.

title: Own metadata next to OME metadata without name clashes
statement: As a tool developer storing my own metadata on OME-Zarr groups,\nI want OME metadata kept under one reserved key,\nso my keys never collide with current or future spec fields.
notes:
0.5: Core: all OME-Zarr metadata lives under attributes.ome (RFC-2), leaving other attribute keys free.
0.6: Core: unchanged.
0.9dev: Core: unchanged.
Forum (123091): vendors proposed three metadata levels: core spec, public machine-readable extensions, and private extensions (to avoid).
Zulip (json-ld and ngff): third-party extension of metadata schemas (JSON-LD, LinkML) discussed.

title: Transforms every viewer can show the same way
statement: As a data producer sharing registered images,\nI want the spec to say which transformations every viewer must support,\nso my data looks the same in most tools, while advanced transforms stay available when needed.
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: only scale and translation exist, so there is nothing advanced to tier.\n0.6: Core: conforming readers MUST parse identity, scale, translation and sequences, SHOULD parse mapAxis, affine, rotation and byDimension, and SHOULD warn about the rest.\n0.9dev: Core: unchanged.

title: Recognize OME-Zarr files by file type
statement: As a researcher using desktop tools,\nI want single-file OME-Zarr to have its own file extension,\nso I can double-click it to open my viewer, the OS does not unzip it in place, and tools know it is OME-Zarr without opening it.
workaround: .zip or .ome.zarr.zip by convention
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no single-file form or extension.
0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.
0.9dev: Out of spec: RFC-9 (in review) proposes .ozx and an archive comment with ome.version.
Forum (91705): tools rely on the .zarr suffix, which Zarr v2 does not require.

title: Read a remote single-file OME-Zarr with few requests
statement: As a data manager serving zipped OME-Zarr over HTTP or S3,\nI want the hierarchy metadata found at a predictable place in the file,\nso clients learn the structure with a few range requests instead of parsing a central directory with every chunk.
workaround: ZIP central directory + HTTP range requests; sharding to keep the directory small
notes:
0.5: Possible: ZIP allows ranged reads, but nothing orders entries or says where metadata is.
0.6: Possible: unchanged.
0.9dev: Possible: RFC-9 (in review) recommends zarr.json entries first, breadth-first, flagged by zipFile.centralDirectory.jsonFirst.
Prior art: ESA distributes Sentinel-2 as zipped Zarr; zarr-python ".zarr.zip on s3".

title: Group single-file images into a collection
statement: As a researcher with many small .ozx images (e.g. a series or a training set),\nI want a collection that points to several single-file OME-Zarrs,\nso I keep one file per image and still open them together.
workaround: Separate files listed in a side file
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no collections and no single-file form.
0.6: Out of spec: scenes reference images by path inside one hierarchy only.
0.9dev: Out of spec: RFC-9 explicitly forbids embedding .ozx in another OME-Zarr; listed as future work with the collections RFC (RFC-8).
Zulip (SpatialData & ZipStore (RFC-9)): zipping individual elements (groups) of a container, not only the root.
Zulip (RFC-9): .ozx HCS plates are already written by some tools although the spec does not cover them yet.

title: Simple single-image files that open without prompts
statement: As a viewer developer,\nI want to know that a file holds exactly one image,\nso I can open it directly without asking the user which part of the hierarchy to load.
workaround: Root group with one multiscales image and no other children
notes: 0.5: Possible: a root multiscales group is one image, but nothing declares that the file holds only that.\n0.6: Possible: unchanged.\n0.9dev: Possible: RFC-9 abandoned a single-volume profile, leaving it as future work ("profiles").

title: Arbitrary key-value metadata
statement: As a data producer with curated metadata (sampling location, date, curated channel info),\nI want to attach arbitrary key-value pairs to an image, like OMERO map annotations,\nso this metadata travels inside the OME-Zarr instead of only in archive file lists.
workaround: Custom attributes; MapAnnotations in OME-XML under the bioformats2raw layout; ro-crate-metadata.json (ome2024 challenge layout)
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no key-value block; custom attributes outside the ome key are allowed but not understood by tools.
0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.
0.9dev: Out of spec: unchanged; RFC-8 extension points may give it a place.
Thread also argues every OME-Zarr SHOULD carry a license.

title: Built-in thumbnails
statement: As a user browsing many OME-Zarrs (galleries, file managers, repository listings),\nI want a small precomputed preview image stored with the data,\nso previews appear instantly, including in OS file browsers, without rendering the pyramid.
workaround: Zarr thumbnails convention (clbarnes/zarr-convention-thumbnails); Zarrcade thumbnails folder
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no thumbnail; viewers render the lowest level.
0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.
0.9dev: Out of spec: a Zarr-level convention is being drafted, independent of OME metadata.
Open question (mkitti): attach thumbnails to arrays, groups, multiscales, wells or the root?

title: Herbarium and other macro specimen scans
statement: As a natural history collection digitizing specimens,\nI want to store large 2D RGB specimen scans as OME-Zarr with collector numbers and specimen identifiers,\nso they can be browsed as pyramids, used for AI, and linked to specimen records (e.g. GBIF).
workaround: EuBI-Bridge conversion; identifiers and catalog links in custom attributes
notes: 0.5/0.6/0.9dev: Awkward: specimen scans are usually JPEG, and without a JPEG codec they must be re-encoded and grow. This is a Zarr codec issue, not OME-Zarr, and the same in every spec version (see STORY-094); the structure (2D RGB multiscales with physical scale) always worked.\n#135: collector numbers and duplicate specimens as a federated way to identify data and credit collectors.\nZulip (Hosting options for ngff): museum object images may not be accepted by bioimage archives.

title: Small local file that points to a remote OME-Zarr
statement: As a biologist working with a dataset too big to download,\nI want a small file holding the remote location (and access details) that tools open like a local image,\nso I can drag it into Fiji, email it or double-click it while the data stays on S3.
workaround: Share the URL
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no reference/proxy file.
0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.
0.9dev: Out of spec: RFC-8 drafts pointers to OME-Zarrs in other locations; idea of an .ozx variant whose data lives externally.
Forum (120640): opening a cloud or local OME-Zarr in Fiji from a web application (fiji:// link).
Forum (123085): viewers (vizarr) reading stores behind access control by being handed a credential.
Forum (72244): private annotations shared as Zarr links with expiring tokens.
Zulip (signed s3 url): pre-signed URLs to private buckets do not work for a directory-like OME-Zarr; workaround: pre-sign each file into a kerchunk JSON.

title: Declare sidecar metadata files
statement: As a metadata harvester or validator,\nI want zarr.json to state that a sidecar metadata file (ro-crate-metadata.json, croissant.json, a table) exists and where,\nso I find it without probing with exploratory requests.
workaround: Fixed file names by convention (ome2024 challenge layout); validator probes for ro-crate-metadata.json
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: nothing in the spec points to sidecar files.
0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.
0.9dev: Out of spec: proposed as a Zarr convention.
Zurich 2026 links discussion: generic links to objects/files (and prefixes like a directory of parquet files) were proposed.

title: Tag images with what they are about
statement: As a curator making images findable (e.g. 'images about genes X, Y and Z'),\nI want to tag any group with identifiers (resolvable URIs) of the things it is about,\nso indexing services can find images by topic without a full metadata model.
workaround: Custom attributes; RO-Crate about
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no keyword or subject field.
0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.
0.9dev: Out of spec: unchanged.
ngff#213 (2026): tags and CURIEs proposed as image-level baseline metadata for search indexing.

title: Persistent identifiers that resolve to an OME-Zarr
statement: As a data publisher,\nI want a DOI to resolve to a landing page whose FAIR Signposting links point to the OME-Zarr bytes,\nso viewers can open data from its persistent identifier and the citation stays stable when storage moves.
workaround: Landing page with Signposting links (lubianat/oz_signpost prototype)
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: no identifier or landing-page link in the spec.\n0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.\n0.9dev: Out of spec: unchanged.

title: Searchable catalogs of OME-Zarr datasets
statement: As a researcher looking for data across repositories,\nI want OME-Zarr datasets described in standard catalog records (like STAC in geospatial),\nso I can search by modality, organism or extent and load matching images directly.
workaround: BioSTAC prototype
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no catalog description.
0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.
0.9dev: Out of spec: unchanged; STAC ideas may inform RFC-7/RFC-8.
Forum (117372): 18,259 single-tile OME-Zarrs submitted to BIA; one tile per OME-Zarr was chosen so images stay findable.

title: RGB images as one color image
statement: As a data producer converting brightfield slides and photographs,\nI want to declare that an image's channels are the R, G, B samples of one color image,\nso that viewers render it as true color with one shared, fixed window, and tools don't have to guess RGB from c=3 and uint8.
workaround: omero channel colours FF0000/00FF00/0000FF with equal windows and rdefs.model "color" (transitional); custom attribute
notes:
0.5: Awkward: only the transitional omero block hints at RGB; OME-TIFF marks it with SamplesPerPixel=3, which is lost in conversion.
0.6: Awkward: unchanged.
0.9dev: Awkward: unchanged.
RFC-7 scoping (ngff#580) proposes photometric interpretation in core, as its own field or by requiring channel IDs R, G, B. d-v-b notes RGBA can also be packed in a struct dtype, which uses the same memory as a channel axis; RFC-7 targets the channel axis but keeps that door open.
Forum (48386): 2021 call: RGB as samples per pixel vs channels, with access patterns (GPU) in mind.

title: Color space of RGB data
statement: As a data producer or analyst working with RGB images from different scanners and cameras,\nI want to record what color space the values are in (a standard name, an embedded ICC profile, or explicitly unknown),\nso that viewers display them consistently, analyses like stain deconvolution are comparable across devices, and a source TIFF's profile isn't lost in conversion.
user_classes: Data producer; Bioimage analyst; Data scientist
workaround: ICC bytes in a namespaced custom attribute or a sidecar .icc; or convert to sRGB at write time and document it
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no colour-space field.
0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.
0.9dev: Out of spec: unchanged.
TIFF has the InterColorProfile tag (34675), but OME-XML doesn't model it and Bio-Formats drops it. DICOM WSI carries an ICC profile (prior art). Some vendors (Hamamatsu NDPI) apply a profile and gamma in their viewer without storing them in the file (image.sc #77414).

title: Register to a specific remote coordinate system
statement: As a researcher registering data to a published atlas,\nI want to point at that atlas's own coordinate system by location or identifier,\nso that my data is aligned to that exact space, not to one that only shares axis names and units.
workaround: Same-named coordinate system copied into each dataset
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: no coordinate systems to reference.\n0.6: Out of spec: coordinate systems are matched by name, within the same hierarchy.\n0.9dev: Out of spec: links to coordinate systems in other stores (e.g. by UUID) under discussion.

title: Link to the original acquisition file
statement: As a data manager converting legacy formats,\nI want an OME-Zarr to reference the original raw file on the same storage,\nso that provenance back to the source file is machine-readable.
workaround: Free-text attribute with the file path
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: no link to non-Zarr objects.\n0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.\n0.9dev: Out of spec: an "object" link type was discussed.

title: Transform parameters stored in external files
statement: As a method developer,\nI want a coordinate transformation to take its parameters from a non-Zarr file (e.g. CSV) or from a slice of one array packing many affine matrices,\nso that existing tool outputs are used without conversion or one array per transform.
workaround: Convert parameters to one Zarr array or inline JSON per transform
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: no coordinate transformations beyond scale/translation.\n0.6: Out of spec: transforms can reference whole Zarr arrays by path only.\n0.9dev: Out of spec: array-subset and object links under discussion.

title: Links that survive moving data
statement: As a data manager depositing OME-Zarr in a repository,\nI want links to other images, labels or files to keep working when the dataset is copied or moved, or to fail visibly when they don't,\nso that published data isn't silently broken or pointing at the wrong object.
workaround: Relative paths only; manual checks before deposition
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: no links beyond relative paths.\n0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.\n0.9dev: Out of spec: RFC-8 links under discussion. Options include the expected ID (e.g. UUID) of the target stated in the link, or resolving through persistent identifiers with FAIR Signposting (STORY-120). Security concerns: external links can be abused (HDF5/HuggingFace case); `..` paths and cycles are risky.

title: Cell tracking graphs linked to segmentations
statement: As a researcher tracking cells in time-lapses,\nI want to store tracks and lineages (divisions, merges) as a graph that points to the segmentation it was built from,\nso that several tracking solutions share one set of labels and tools can stream them with the images.
workaround: GEFF files next to the OME-Zarr; CTC lineage text files; relabelling segmentations by track ID
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: no graph or track data.\n0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.\n0.9dev: Out of spec: GEFF as an RFC-8 extension was drafted at the Zurich 2026 hackathon.

title: Plates re-imaged over days
statement: As a screening scientist imaging the same plates at set intervals (e.g. daily),\nI want to add each new acquisition to the existing plate,\nso that I can browse and analyse the plate over time without rewriting earlier data.
workaround: Pre-allocate an oversized time axis and fill it; or store each day as an extra field/acquisition
notes: 0.5: Awkward: either a pre-sized t axis or one field per acquisition; viewers often load only the first field.\n0.6: Awkward: unchanged.\n0.9dev: Awkward: RFC-8 collections may group acquisitions, but time order is not defined.

title: Same image stored with several chunk layouts
statement: As a data provider serving both 2D slice browsing and 3D analysis,\nI want to store the same image with more than one chunk layout and say which is which,\nso that each tool reads the layout that suits it.
workaround: Several multiscales in one group, told apart by name only
notes:
0.5: Awkward: several multiscales are allowed, but only a name says what each is.
0.6: Awkward: unchanged.
0.9dev: Awkward: collections could group them; no way to say they hold the same data.
Zulip (OME-Zarr 0.6): multiple multiscales for 3D views with other chunkings; test data with several multiscales opened in no tool.

title: Tile, angle and illumination of each view
statement: As a developer of light-sheet tools (e.g. BigDataViewer, BigStitcher),\nI want each view of a multi-view acquisition to state its tile, angle, illumination and channel,\nso that users can select views like 'all of tile 3' and tools can add their own view attributes.
workaround: BigDataViewer XML (SpimData) or OME-XML next to the data
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: only OME-XML via bioformats2raw.\n0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.\n0.9dev: Out of spec: RFC-8 attributes could hold them, none defined.

title: Sample and treatment metadata for reuse
statement: As a researcher reusing public cell biology images,\nI want each image to say which sample and treatment it shows (including which are controls) and what is labelled, using database identifiers,\nso that I can address new biological questions with the data.
workaround: OME-XML annotations, custom attributes, or repository metadata (e.g. REMBI in BIA)
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no sample or treatment fields.
0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.
0.9dev: Out of spec: tagging with identifiers is proposed (STORY-119), no sample/treatment model.
Zulip (Adding New Information into a Tiff File/OME-Zarr): storing the staining protocol (e.g. H&E) with the image instead of in separate documents.

title: Overview image with higher-resolution regions
statement: As an electron or light microscopist imaging a large area at low resolution and selected regions at high resolution,\nI want to store them in one image where the high-resolution data exists only in those regions,\nso that viewers show the overview everywhere and detail where it was acquired, without padding or one layer per tile.
workaround: Pad the high-resolution level with empty chunks; or store each region as its own image
notes: 0.5: Awkward: a padded sparse pyramid works on disk, but nothing says which region is filled, and missing chunks are not shown as transparent.\n0.6: Possible: an RFC-5 scene can place high- and low-resolution images in one coordinate system, but each region becomes its own image and viewer layer.\n0.9dev: Possible: same as 0.6.

title: Know whether a dataset was written completely
statement: As a data producer or manager writing or uploading large OME-Zarrs,\nI want a simple way to tell whether a dataset was written completely,\nso that interrupted writes or uploads are not mistaken for finished data.
workaround: Write OME metadata last; checksum manifests or upload logs
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: missing chunks are indistinguishable from fill values; no completion marker.
0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.
0.9dev: Out of spec: unchanged.
Zulip (reading Zarr that is being written in Java): a reader cannot tell a chunk not yet written from an empty one.

title: Processing history stored with the data
statement: As a bioimage analyst running workflows (Fractal, Nextflow, napari, Fiji),\nI want every tool that changes an OME-Zarr to record the step it ran, with tool, version and parameters,\nso that results can be reproduced and datasets found by how they were processed (e.g. 'Cellpose with an explicit diameter').
user_classes: Bioimage analyst; Tool developer; Data manager
workaround: Workflow RO-Crates (nf-prov), tool logs, custom attributes
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: no provenance metadata.\n0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.\n0.9dev: Out of spec: a 'provenance' Zarr convention and a bioimage task vocabulary are being drafted.

title: Compact non-rigid transforms
statement: As a researcher registering large volumes,\nI want to store B-spline control grids or blended local affines (polyaffine),\nso that a deformation stays kilobytes instead of a sampled field of many gigabytes.
workaround: Sample the deformation into a dense displacement field; keep ITK transform files beside the data
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: no non-linear transforms.\n0.6: Awkward: only a dense displacements field; a 1,296-parameter B-spline becomes ~18 GB.\n0.9dev: Awkward: RFC-8 makes transforms an extension point, none defined.

title: Downsampling method of pyramid levels
statement: As a tool developer building pyramids of intensity and label images,\nI want each level to record how it was downsampled (mean, Gaussian, mode, nearest),\nso that label levels stay valid, viewers place levels correctly, and analysts know whether small objects survive.
workaround: Free-form multiscales 'type' and 'metadata' fields; tool conventions
notes:
0.5: Possible: optional free-form 'type' and 'metadata' on multiscales, but no defined values.
0.6: Possible: unchanged.
0.9dev: Possible: unchanged.
zarr-specs#50 (2020): the first multiscales draft proposed a 'type' enumeration (gaussian, laplacian, reduce, pick) plus method metadata; it never became binding.
Zulip (downsampling and translation): whether a level needs a translation depends on the sampling grid ('sample' vs 'average' in the Fiji exporter); the long disagreement shows the method and grid need recording.

title: Several pyramids from one base array
statement: As a tool developer generating pyramids,\nI want to build more than one pyramid (e.g. Gaussian and Laplacian, or mean and mode) from the same full-resolution array,\nso that each use gets the pyramid it needs without copying the base data.
workaround: Copy the base array into a second image group; or keep one pyramid only
notes:
0.5: Possible: `multiscales` is a list; entries can share `datasets` paths and differ by `name`/`type`. Readers pick by name, falling back to the first.
0.6: Possible: unchanged.
0.9dev: Unsure: RFC-8 makes the multiscale node a single object (absorbing the retracted RFC-6); whether two multiscale nodes can share one base array is unclear.
Never observed in practice (image.sc 103267; Zulip 'multiscales: spec vs de-facto', 2026). Most readers reportedly use only the first entry; ome-ngff-validator lists them all.

title: Several metadata versions over the same arrays
statement: As a data provider moving to a new OME-Zarr version,\nI want metadata for the old and new spec versions side by side over the same arrays,\nso that readers that understand only one version still open the data while tools catch up, without copying chunks.
user_classes: Data provider; Tool developer; Data manager
workaround: Nested groups, one per version, pointing at shared arrays; symlinked chunk folders; a store that maps alternative zarr.json names; Icechunk branches
notes:
0.5: Awkward: a node has one zarr.json with one `ome` version, so two versions can never share the same path. It works only by bending the layout: nest groups, each declaring one version, with the outer group's dataset paths pointing down to the inner group's arrays (each version then opens at a different path); 0.4 (Zarr v2 .zattrs) and 0.5 (zarr.json) files can also sit in one folder over shared chunks, because each Zarr version reads only its own files.
0.6: Awkward: same; 0.5 and 0.6 are both Zarr v3, so only the nested-group hack applies.
0.9dev: Unsure: RFC-8 may change how nodes reference arrays.
Zulip (Same data, different metdata): without this, users must choose between old and new metadata and risk tools not reading their data; an `ome` value holding several versions was floated.

title: Images linked to other assays of the same sample
statement: As a researcher with imaging, proteomics and metabolomics from the same parent sample, acquired separately,\nI want to link or bundle the OME-Zarr images with the other assays and keep their acquisition metadata consistent,\nso that all modalities of one sample are found and analysed together despite different metadata schemas.
workaround: Shared sample identifiers in custom attributes; separate files linked by naming
notes: 0.5: Out of spec: no way to point to non-image assays.\n0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.\n0.9dev: Unsure: RFC-8 collections group nodes; whether AnnData or other assay files can be members is unclear.

title: Acquisition date of images
statement: As a researcher,\nI want each image to record the date and time it was acquired,\nso that images from different sessions can be ordered, compared and placed on the experiment's timeline.
workaround: OME-XML Image AcquisitionDate in the bioformats2raw layout; custom attributes
notes:
0.5: Out of spec: no acquisition date field. OME-XML has AcquisitionDate and can sit in `OME/METADATA.ome.xml` (bioformats2raw layout), but OME-Zarr readers do not read it.
0.6: Out of spec: unchanged.
0.9dev: Out of spec: unchanged.
Differs from STORY-002 (time of each frame within a time lapse) and STORY-001 (metadata attached to time points).
Zulip (potential RFC: coordinate arrays): described as basic functionality.
